units.source: Default Themes__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Themes > Default Themes

units.source: Trilium comes with a couple pre-installed color themes, with the default being a light theme. To switch to a dark theme or any other available theme, navigate to the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ Options menu (accessible via the app icon in the top-left corner), select the Appearance tab, and choose your preferred theme. The __TRILIUM_PH_1__Theme__TRILIUM_PH_2__ submenu of the __TRILIUM_PH_3__Global menu__TRILIUM_PH_4__ switches the theme and the color scheme as well.
units.context: Themes > Default Themes

units.source: While a dark theme is active, Trilium asks the Dark Reader browser extension not to darken the page a second time. Dark Reader still darkens the light themes. After switching from a dark theme to a light one, reload the page (__TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__+__TRILIUM_PH_2__R__TRILIUM_PH_3__) for Dark Reader to take effect again.
units.context: Themes > Default Themes

units.source: Creating Custom CSS Themes__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Themes > Creating Custom CSS Themes

units.source: Trilium supports custom user themes, allowing you to personalize the application's appearance. To create a custom theme, follow these steps:
units.context: Themes > Creating Custom CSS Themes

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Create a CSS Code Note__TRILIUM_PH_1__: Start by creating a new __TRILIUM_PH_2__code note__TRILIUM_PH_3__ with the __TRILIUM_PH_4__ type.
units.context: Themes > Creating Custom CSS Themes

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Annotate with__TRILIUM_PH_1__ __TRILIUM_PH_2__: Add the __TRILIUM_PH_3__attribute__TRILIUM_PH_4__ __TRILIUM_PH_5__ to your note, where __TRILIUM_PH_6__ is the name of your custom theme.
units.context: Themes > Creating Custom CSS Themes

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Define Your Styles__TRILIUM_PH_1__: Write your custom CSS within the note.
units.context: Themes > Creating Custom CSS Themes

units.source: Activating Your Custom Theme__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Themes > Creating Custom CSS Themes > Activating Your Custom Theme

units.source: Once you've created your custom theme:
units.context: Themes > Creating Custom CSS Themes > Activating Your Custom Theme

units.source: Go to "Menu" -> "Options" (__TRILIUM_PH_0__) -> "Appearance."
units.context: Themes > Creating Custom CSS Themes > Activating Your Custom Theme

units.source: In the theme selection dropdown, you should see your custom theme listed under the name you provided with the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__label__TRILIUM_PH_2__.
units.context: Themes > Creating Custom CSS Themes > Activating Your Custom Theme

units.source: Select your custom theme to activate it.
units.context: Themes > Creating Custom CSS Themes > Activating Your Custom Theme

units.source: Your custom theme is also listed under __TRILIUM_PH_0__Global menu__TRILIUM_PH_1__ → __TRILIUM_PH_2__Theme__TRILIUM_PH_3__, with the icon of its note.
units.context: Themes > Creating Custom CSS Themes > Activating Your Custom Theme

units.source: If you make changes to your theme, press Ctrl + R to reload the frontend and apply your updates.
units.context: Themes > Creating Custom CSS Themes > Activating Your Custom Theme

units.source: Sharing and Importing Themes__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Themes > Creating Custom CSS Themes > Sharing and Importing Themes

units.source: Custom themes can be exported as __TRILIUM_PH_0__ archives, which can be shared with other users. However, be cautious when importing themes from untrusted sources, as they may contain executable scripts that could pose security risks.
units.context: Themes > Creating Custom CSS Themes > Sharing and Importing Themes

units.source: An example user theme, __TRILIUM_PH_0__Steel Blue__TRILIUM_PH_1__, is available in the demo document.
units.context: Themes > Creating Custom CSS Themes > Sharing and Importing Themes

units.source: Using Custom CSS for Specific Purposes__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Themes > Creating Custom CSS Themes > Using Custom CSS for Specific Purposes

units.source: In addition to full themes, Trilium allows for custom CSS that isn't tied to a theme. This can be particularly useful in scripting contexts, where you might want to modify specific UI elements, such as changing the colors of notes in the tree view.
units.context: Themes > Creating Custom CSS Themes > Using Custom CSS for Specific Purposes

units.source: User-Provided Themes__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Themes > Creating Custom CSS Themes > User-Provided Themes

units.source: A gallery of user-created themes is available, showcasing the variety of customizations that the Trilium community has developed. For more information, check the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Theme Gallery__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
units.context: Themes > Creating Custom CSS Themes > User-Provided Themes

units.source: Asset Path Management__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Themes > Creating Custom CSS Themes > Asset Path Management

units.source: When referencing built-in assets like images in your custom themes or CSS, you can avoid hardcoding version numbers by using the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ alias. For example, instead of specifying __TRILIUM_PH_1__, you can use __TRILIUM_PH_2__ to keep your theme compatible with future versions of Trilium.
units.context: Themes > Creating Custom CSS Themes > Asset Path Management
